tool.name: OPERA
tool.description: - QSAR predictions of physicochemical, environmental fate, ADME and toxicity endpoints
tool.command:
## --------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## OPERA picks its input parser from the *extension* of the input file ## (.sdf/.mol/.smi/.txt) and Galaxy dataset paths carry no extension, so link ## the input to a file name with the extension OPERA expects. ## --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #if str($input_source.input_type) == "structures": #set $input_name = 'opera_input.' + str($input_source.input_format) ln -s '$input_source.input_file' '$input_name' && #end if
## --------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Output location. With -x OPERA does NOT write the requested file but one ## file per endpoint named <output>_<Endpoint>.<ext>, so point it into a ## dedicated directory which is then harvested as a collection. ## --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #set $out_ext = str($output_format) #if str($separate_outputs) == '-x': mkdir -p 'separate' && #set $out_path = 'separate/predictions.' + $out_ext #else: #set $out_path = 'predictions.' + $out_ext #end if
@RUN_SCRIPT@ @MCR_DIR@
## ------------------------------- Input ------------------------------------- #if str($input_source.input_type) == "structures": -s '$input_name' #else -d '$input_source.descriptor_file' #if $input_source.molid_file -i '$input_source.molid_file' #end if #if $input_source.labels_file -l '$input_source.labels_file' #end if #end if $standardize #if $salt_info -t '$salt_info' #end if
## ----------------------------- Endpoints ----------------------------------- #set $mode = str($endpoint_selector.endpoint_mode) #if $mode == "group" and $endpoint_selector.endpoint_group #for $group in $endpoint_selector.endpoint_group -$group #end for #elif $mode == "custom" and $endpoint_selector.endpoints -e #for $endpoint in $endpoint_selector.endpoints $endpoint #end for #else -a #end if
## ------------------------------ Output ------------------------------------- #if str($full_output) == '-O' -O '$out_path' #else -o '$out_path' #end if $separate_outputs $include_neighbors $get_descriptors $experimental
## ---------------------------- Miscellaneous -------------------------------- $clean_temp -v $verbose
## --------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## MATLAB can exit 0 after a silent failure; make sure something was written. ## --------------------------------------------------------------------------- && #if str($separate_outputs) == '-x': ls separate/*.csv > /dev/null #else: test -s '$out_path' #end if

param.name: input_type
param.label: Input data type
param.help: OPERA predicts either from chemical structures/identifiers (descriptors are then calculated internally with PaDEL-Descriptor and CDK) or from pre-calculated PaDEL descriptors

param.name: input_file
param.label: Chemical structures or identifiers
param.help: (-s) SDF/MOL (v2000), a tab-delimited SMILES file, or a text file with one CASRN/DTXSID/DTXCID/InChIKey per line. Organic molecules only; MW <= 2000 g/mol; <= 100 heavy atoms; no mixtures, UVCBs or nanomaterials.

param.name: input_format
param.label: Input file format
param.help: OPERA selects the parser from the file extension, which Galaxy dataset names do not carry, so it has to be declared here
param.option: SDF - structure file in v2000 format (single or multiple structures)
MOL - single structure in v2000 MOL format
SMILES - tab-delimited text, optionally with molecule names; no header and no empty lines
Identifiers - one CASRN, DTXSID, DTXCID or InChIKey per line; no header and no empty lines

param.label: Generate QSAR-ready structures before predicting
param.help: (-st) Runs the bundled KNIME QSAR-ready workflow to standardize and desalt the input structures. Improves predictions (salt information is derived automatically) but is slow and needs the KNIME workflow shipped with the OPERA installer.

param.name: descriptor_file
param.label: Pre-calculated PaDEL descriptors (CSV)
param.help: (-d) Standard PaDEL 2D descriptor output; the first column should be named 'Name' and hold the molecule identifiers, otherwise generic IDs are assigned. Note that pKa/LogD additionally require PaDEL fingerprints and CERAPP/CoMPARA/CATMoS/FuB/Clint/Caco2 additionally require CDK 2.0 descriptors, so those endpoints cannot be predicted from a PaDEL-only descriptor file.

param.name: molid_file
param.label: Molecule names (optional)
param.help: (-i) Molecule identifiers, one per row, in the same order as the descriptor file. Used when the descriptor file has no 'Name' column.

param.name: labels_file
param.label: Descriptor labels (optional)
param.help: (-l) Descriptor names, one per column. Required if the descriptor file carries no header or contains more than the 1444 PaDEL 2D descriptors.

param.name: salt_info
param.label: Salt information (optional)
param.help: (-t) Salt IDs, one per molecule, used to improve the LogP, MP, BP, VP, WS, LogD and CATMoS predictions. The list of valid IDs is provided in Salts.xls of the OPERA installation.

param.name: endpoint_mode
param.label: Endpoints to predict
param.option: All endpoints (structural, physicochemical, environmental fate, ADME and toxicity)

param.name: endpoints
param.label: Endpoints
param.help: Descriptors are calculated once and shared by all selected endpoints, so predicting several endpoints in one run is much cheaper than running the tool several times.

param.name: output_format
param.label: Output format
param.help: OPERA derives the format from the extension of the requested output file

param.name: separate_outputs
param.label: Write a separate output file for each endpoint
param.help: (-x) Recommended when predicting many molecules; the per-endpoint files are returned as additional datasets.

param.name: include_neighbors
param.label: Include the 5 nearest neighbours from the training set
param.help: (-n) Adds the CAS numbers, InChIKeys and DTXSIDs of the nearest neighbours together with their observed and predicted values.

param.name: full_output
param.label: Full output: all prediction details, nearest neighbours and used descriptors
param.help: (-O) Equivalent to combining 'Include the 5 nearest neighbours' and 'Include used descriptors'. Only available for CSV output.

param.name: get_descriptors
param.label: Append the descriptors used by the models to the output
param.help: (-gd) The descriptor values are appended as additional columns of the predictions table.

param.name: experimental
param.label: Include experimental values where available
param.help: (-exp) Requires CASRN or DTXSID identifiers in the input; free-form molecule names are not enough.

param.name: clean_temp
param.label: Remove the temporary descriptor files
param.help: (-c) Deletes the PaDEL/CDK descriptor files generated during the run.

param.name: verbose
param.label: Verbose level
param.help: Controls how much detail is written to the job log

tool.help:
## What it does
**OPERA** is a free, open-source and open-data suite of **QSAR** (quantitative structure–activity relationship) models developed at the U.S. EPA / NIEHS. For a list of chemicals it predicts around **30 endpoints** covering general structural properties, physicochemical properties, environmental fate, ADME and toxicity — including the CERAPP (estrogen receptor), CoMPARA (androgen receptor) and CATMoS (acute oral toxicity) consensus models.
Every single prediction is reported together with:
| Column | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `<endpoint>_pred` | The predicted value | | `<endpoint>_predRange` | The predicted range (accuracy interval) | | `<endpoint>_AD` | Applicability domain flag: `1` = inside, `0` = outside | | `<endpoint>_AD_index` | Applicability domain index (0-1, higher = more similar to the training set) | | `<endpoint>_Conf_index` | Confidence / accuracy estimate (0-1) |
Each model has a published **QMRF** (Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship Model Reporting Format) in the JRC QSAR Model Database: <https://qsardb.jrc.ec.europa.eu/qmrf/endpoint>.
## Input
OPERA accepts one of:
- **SDF / MOL** — structures in MDL v2000 format (single or multiple records). - **SMILES** — a tab-delimited text file `SMILES[<TAB>name]`, with **no header and no empty lines**. Molecule names are optional; generic `AUTOGEN_n` IDs are assigned when they are missing. - **Identifiers** — a text file with one **CASRN**, **DTXSID**, **DTXCID** or **InChIKey** per line (no header, no empty lines). Structures are resolved against the QSAR-ready database shipped with OPERA and the `FoundBy` column reports how each structure was found (`NotFound` marks unresolved IDs). - **Pre-calculated PaDEL descriptors** — the standard PaDEL 2D descriptor CSV. pKa/LogD additionally require PaDEL fingerprints and CERAPP/CoMPARA/CATMoS/FuB/Clint/Caco2 additionally require CDK 2.0 descriptors, so those endpoints cannot be predicted from a PaDEL-only descriptor file.
Because OPERA chooses its parser from the **file extension**, please confirm the *Input file format* — Galaxy dataset names do not carry an extension.
**Hard limits** (organics only): molecular weight ≤ 2000 g/mol, ≤ 100 heavy atoms, and no mixtures, UVCBs or nanomaterials.
## Endpoints
@ENDPOINT_TABLE@
Choose **All endpoints**, whole **groups** (`StrP`, `PC`, `EF`, `Tox`, `ADME`) or individual endpoints.
## Output
By default a single table is produced with the molecule ID followed by the prediction, applicability-domain and confidence columns of every requested endpoint.
- **Separate output file for each endpoint** (`-x`) returns one dataset per endpoint — recommended for large input sets. - **TXT** output produces the human-readable OPERA report instead of a table. - **Include experimental values** (`-exp`) adds `<endpoint>_exp` columns; this requires CASRN or DTXSID identifiers in the input. - **Full output** (`-O`) additionally appends the nearest neighbours and the descriptor values used by the models (CSV only).
## Notes
- OPERA runs **fully offline**: the models and the reference databases are part of the installation and the application has no access to the web. - Salt information materially improves the LogP, MP, BP, VP, WS, LogD and CATMoS predictions. It is retrieved automatically when the input contains CASRN or DTXSID identifiers, when *Generate QSAR-ready structures* is enabled, or when a salt-information file is supplied; otherwise OPERA warns that predictions may be affected. - The **serial** OPERA build is wrapped here. The parallel build (`OPERA_par`) is a different installer and does not accept the same argument list, so it is not exposed by this tool.
@ATTRIBUTION@
